source_map.content: Candidate-only evaluation can hide retrieval behavior.
An aggregate full-flow outcome does not localize retrieval, selection, or coverage-tracking failure.
Crawler, selector, and coverage controller have distinct responsibilities.
No benchmark values or causal performance evidence are available.

paper_thesis: The synthetic brief motivates separating diagnostic failure loci and method responsibilities without making an empirical performance claim.

claims.text: Candidate-only evaluation can hide retrieval behavior.
claims.evidence: The brief states this limitation directly.
claims.visual_implication: Show retrieval visibility as one bounded diagnostic problem.

claims.text: A single full-flow outcome does not identify which of three named loci failed.
claims.evidence: The brief distinguishes retrieval, selection, and coverage tracking.
claims.visual_implication: Use parallel diagnostic regions without sequential arrows.
claims.must_not_imply: The three failures always occur together or in sequence.

claims.text: Crawler, selector, and coverage controller have separate high-level responsibilities.
claims.evidence: The brief assigns acquisition, prioritization, and scope tracking to the three responsibilities.
claims.visual_implication: Use distinct modules and only supported procedural handoffs.
claims.must_not_imply: The modules guarantee better benchmark performance.

claims.visual_implication: Do not render a result panel.

missing_evidence: Machine-readable benchmark results and uncertainty are required before planning an experiment figure.
